prompt1: Home schooling proposals spark ‘abuser’s charter’ warning 24/11/2024 – Freddie Whittaker, journalist, Schools Week  Proposals requiring families of children subject to protection enquiries to get council consent for home education risk creating an “abuser’s charter”, the government has been warned. Bridget Phillipson, the education secretary, announced this week that she would legislate for new powers and protections for children in the social care system. Under one proposal, families of children subject to child protection enquiries or plans will need local authority consent to withdraw their children to educate them at home. The law would also give councils the power to require children already in home education to attend school if they become subject to an enquiry or plan. Wendy Charles-Warner, of home education campaign group Education Otherwise, said it was “perfectly reasonable” to require consent for those with child protection plans. But including those who are subject to protection enquiries would “lead to any child referred to children’s social services for assessment being subject to (presumably) a school attendance order, regardless of the outcome of that referral”. Charles-Warner said the new law risked becoming an “abuser’s charter”. She added: “This will also lead to abusive former partners or individuals seeking to harass families making nuisance-mongering referrals in order to exploit the provision to further their abuse and harassment.”  - what does abusers charter means

You can also share the app with others, but will need to share the password and create separate profiles for each student. The instructors will not be able to help you coordinate with other students if you choose to share the Diet and Wellness Plus+ app purchase. See the Course Resources syllabus page for more detailed information on how to purchase the software.  Recording Food Intake and Activity:  Using the Diet and Wellness Plus+ software you are to record and analyze your food intake and physical activity for three days. We have posted two demos of how to navigate the App to enter your food and activity information and generate reports.  For food intake, record all the food you eat and drink for three days, one of which must be a weekend day. Be sure to record portion sizes as well as what you ate. It is important that you enter your personal profile information BEFORE you enter foods. If you do not, you will have to re-enter the foods after you create your personal profile.  You will also record daily physical activity for the same three days. Please be sure to record the day, time, duration, and intensity of your activities using the criteria in the Diet and Wellness App. These activities should be anything you consider to be above and beyond normal daily 'routine activities'. What we mean by 'routine activities' are those basic activities that can be considered associated with BMR for the average sedentary person. So for example, we DO NOT want you to add up the times you get off the couch, the time spent watching a screen, activity associated with making your bed, making dinner, or walking to your bedroom for a nap. These activities would be captured with BMR. However, you should include all voluntary activities that normal sedentary people would not do. For example, DO include time spent studying (a lot more brain energy used than watching a show!), time spent cleaning the house, walking the dog, raking the lawn, walking to the store for a bag of chips, or playing charades. The more the better, but try to think of these activities as 'voluntary' activities that normal sedentary people would not do.  **NOTE**: If tracking your diet or physical activity is a sensitive activity for you or uncomfortable in any way, please contact the instructors to discuss alternative methods to complete the assignment.  Reports:  In order to complete the Written Evaluation, you will first need to generate two reports from the software: 3-Day  Average and Energy Balance. These reports will sum up various aspects of your diet and physical activity  relative to requirements and give you what you need to answer the questions in the written evaluation. For the  physical activity record, remember to use the same dates as the food intake record. By using the same dates,  the App will calculate energy balance automatically in the report. Discuss the nutrients in your assessment that you believe differ significantly from the DRI - this could be either a very high intake or a low intake relative to the DRI. Submission  When you submit your assignment, it must include:  1. A PDF of the 3-Day Average report. SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit) is a cryptographic hash function that generates a fixed-size 256-bit (32-byte) hash value from an input of any size. It is part of the SHA-2 (Secure Hash Algorithm 2) family, designed by the National Security Agency (NSA) and published by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).  How Does SHA-256 Work? Message Preprocessing:  Padding: The original message is padded to ensure its length is congruent to 448 modulo 512. Padding involves appending a single '1' bit followed by enough '0' bits to make the length of the padded message 64 bits less than a multiple of 512. Length Addition: A 64-bit representation of the original message length (before padding) is appended to the padded message. Initialize Hash Values:  Eight 32-bit words (constants) are used as initial hash values. These values are derived from the first 32 bits of the fractional parts of the square roots of the first eight prime numbers. Processing the Message in Blocks:  The padded message is divided into 512-bit blocks. Each block is processed using a series of logical functions and bitwise operations, involving constants derived from the first 32 bits of the fractional parts of the cube roots of the first 64 prime numbers. Compression Function:  The main loop processes each 512-bit block, updating the intermediate hash values using bitwise operations, modular addition, and logical functions. This process involves message schedule arrays, working variables, and functions such as Sigma and Ch. Final Hash Value:  After processing all blocks, the final hash value is produced by concatenating the updated hash values. Example Code in Python Here's a simple example of using Python's hashlib library to compute the SHA-256 hash of a given input string:  python Copy Edit import hashlib  def compute_sha256_hash(input_string):     # Create a sha256 hash object     sha256_hash = hashlib.sha256()          # Update the hash object with the bytes of the input string     sha256_hash.update(input_string.encode('utf-8'))          # Retrieve the hexadecimal representation of the digest     hash_hex = sha256_hash.hexdigest()          return hash_hex  # Example usage input_string = "Hello, world!" hash_result = compute_sha256_hash(input_string) print(f"SHA-256 hash of '{input_string}': {hash_result}") Explanation of the Code Import the hashlib Library:  The hashlib library in Python provides a common interface to many secure hash and message digest algorithms. Create a SHA-256 Hash Object:  hashlib.sha256() creates a new SHA-256 hash object. Update the Hash Object:  The update method updates the hash object with the bytes of the input string. The encode('utf-8') method converts the input string to bytes using UTF-8 encoding. Retrieve the Hexadecimal Digest:  The hexdigest method returns the digest of the data passed to the update method so far. This is a string of double length, containing only hexadecimal digits. The tagline—“Kamala is for they/them. President Trump is for you.”—could go down in history as one of the most effective campaign slogans ever devised.  The ad reinforced a promise Trump repeated at rally after rally as he toured the swing states: If returned to office, he would immediately take on the gender ideology the Biden administration had embraced. Namely, he would end policies such as allowing males on women’s sports teams and in women’s locker rooms, and the housing of male prisoners who identify as transwomen in federal prisons for female offenders.  President Trump has addressed all this and more in an expansive executive order he will sign tomorrow afternoon called “Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government.”  Here is what the order sets out:  The Executive Order establishes Government-wide the biological reality of two sexes and clearly defines male and female.  All radical gender ideology guidance, communication, policies, and forms are removed.  Agencies will cease pretending that men can be women and women can be men when enforcing laws that protect against sex discrimination.  “Woman” means an “adult human female.”  The Executive Order directs that Government identification like passports and personnel records will reflect biological reality and not self-assessed gender identity.  The Executive Order ends the practice of housing men in women’s prisons and taxpayer funded “transition” for male prisoners.  The Executive Order ends the forced recitation of “preferred pronouns” and protects Americans’ First Amendment and statutory rights to recognize the biological and binary nature of sex.  This includes protection in the workplace and in federal funded entities like schools.  Asked why Trump is making sex-based policy a day one priority of his administration, an incoming senior administration official said, “This really was a defining issue of the campaign. The president is going to be fulfilling the promises he made on the trail.” The executive order puts it more bluntly: “Radical gender ideology has devastated biological truth and women’s safety and opportunity.”  It is becoming something of a presidential tradition to begin a term with sweeping directives regarding “gender identity.” President Biden, on his first day in office, demanded the federal government “review all existing orders, regulations, guidance documents, policies, programs, or other agency actions” that could impinge on transgender rights. Language and rules about transgender identities became embedded in the vast federal bureaucracy.  Now, Trump has ordered a reversal of all this. In an exclusive briefing with The Free Press, two senior officials provided a summary of the executive order. “Women deserve protections, they deserve dignity, they deserve fairness, they deserve safety,” said a senior policy adviser explaining why the order explicitly embraces the necessity of special treatment for women. “And so this is going to help establish that in federal policy and in federal laws.”  In reading the order, it’s clear that lawsuits challenging the new directives will start stacking up quickly. The order, for example, asserts that “All radical gender ideology guidance, communication, policies, and forms are removed.” This is far from mere symbolism. United States passports—which since 2022 have allowed citizens to choose “X” as their gender—will revert to offering exclusively male and female options, with the proviso that what people select must “reflect biological reality and not self-assessed gender identity.”  The executive order also “ends the forced recitation of ‘preferred pronouns’ and protects Americans’ First Amendment and statutory rights to recognize the biological and binary nature of sex.” When asked about how this would affect public universities, which are bound by the First Amendment’s free speech protections, the senior policy adviser said the U.S. attorney general will enforce these rights. The adviser cited a 2022 federal court ruling to the effect that a Shawnee State University philosophy professor was deprived of his First Amendment rights by being forced to address a transgender student using that student’s chosen pronouns.  The task of the Trump administration now will be to promulgate rules implementing the order, which will affect people’s daily lives. It is inevitable that activist organizations will take these matters to court. The policy adviser said the administration is ready for litigation, predicting Trump will be “100 percent successful.”  It’s a fight the new administration seems to relish. Both officials said the executive order has the potential to broaden the president’s support. “Just take a look at the polling,” the senior official said. “The public is broadly in favor of the president’s and of the Republican Party’s stance on gender. That there are two biological sexes is something that the public is supportive of.”  The executive order does not address one of the most contentious areas of transgender activism: “gender-affirming care” for minors, meaning putting gender-distressed young people on a swift course to transition and lifetime medication. The Biden administration ardently supported such treatments, even as other Western nations began to restrict them, and dozens of U.S. states began to ban them.  The Biden administration sued Tennessee over its ban. That case resulted in a contentious oral argument at the Supreme Court in December, after which most observers felt the court would probably uphold Tennessee’s law.  Asked about why the new executive order does not deal with this, the senior official said, “This executive order is the first of many. I would expect that anything the president said he would do on the trail regarding these issues, he’s going to be fulfilling those promises.”  The order ends with a sweeping statement about the fundamental issue the White House believes is at stake in this order: “Men and women are equal but have obvious sexual differences,” it reads. “If federal policies promote such an obvious falsehood that men can become women, the government will forfeit all credibility. The government must maintain a commitment to recognizing biological reality to maintain the trust of the American people.”  This order is one of nearly 200 executive actions the White House is rolling out today. Among them: orders to declare a national emergency at the border; end all DEI programs across the federal government; withdrawal from the Paris climate accord; and a return-to-office directive for federal workers. The Treaty of Apamea that followed ended Seleucid ambitions in the eastern Mediterranean.    368 CE: Battle of Solicinium   Roman forces faced an Alemanni invasion in the area of Solicinium, likely in modern Germany.   Valentinian I directed his troops to block the invaders’ advance into Roman-held Gaul.   The victory was hard-won but reinforced the frontier along the Rhine.    410 CE: Council of Seleucia-Ctesiphon   Church leaders in Persia convened at Seleucia-Ctesiphon under the approval of the Sassanid ruler. This council marked a turning point in the independence of Persian Christianity from the Roman Church.    260 BCE: Battle of Mylae   Rome’s fleet encountered Carthaginian ships off the northern coast of Sicily. prompt8: what is the difference between a loop and recursion? ChatGPT said: ChatGPT  A loop and recursion are both control flow mechanisms used in programming to perform repetitive tasks, but they differ in their approach and implementation. Here's a comparison: 1. Definition      Loop: A control structure that repeatedly executes a block of code as long as a condition is true. Examples include for, while, and do-while loops.     Recursion: A function that calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem, with a base case to terminate the process.  2. Structure      Loop:         Iterative approach.         Involves a counter or condition to terminate the repetition.         Example (Python):      for i in range(5):         print(i)  # Prints 0 to 4  Recursion:      Function-based approach.     Requires a base case to stop the recursion.     Example (Python):          def print_numbers(n):             if n == 0:                 return             print_numbers(n - 1)             print(n)         print_numbers(5)  # Prints 1 to 5  3. Termination      Loop: Ends when the condition in the loop is no longer true.     Recursion: Ends when the base case is met, preventing further self-calls.  4. Memory Usage      Loop:         Generally more memory-efficient as it uses a single block of memory for the entire process.     Recursion:         Uses the call stack, allocating memory for each recursive call. This can lead to stack overflow if the recursion depth is too high.  5. Use Cases      Loop: Ideal for tasks with a known number of iterations or straightforward repetitive actions, such as iterating over an array or counting numbers.     Recursion: Useful for problems that can be divided into smaller subproblems, such as:         Tree traversal (e.g., binary tree).         Calculating factorials.         Solving problems using divide-and-conquer techniques (e.g., quicksort, mergesort).  6. Code Simplicity      Loop: Easier to understand and debug for iterative processes.     Recursion: Can simplify code for complex problems by reducing it to smaller, identical subproblems.  Summary Table: Aspect	Loop	Recursion Approach	Iterative	Function-based Termination	Condition-driven	Base case Memory Usage	Efficient	Higher (uses call stack) Complexity	Easy for iterations	Simplifies subproblem tasks Risk	Infinite loop	Stack overflow Example Use	Counting, array processing	Tree traversal, divide-and-conquer  In practice, loops are typically preferred for performance, while recursion is favored for clarity in specific problem domains.

prompt2: You said: Python functions teach me function recursion ChatGPT said: ChatGPT  Function recursion occurs when a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of the same problem. It's a powerful concept in programming used for tasks that can be broken down into simpler, repetitive sub-tasks.  Here’s a step-by-step explanation with examples: 1. Basic Structure of a Recursive Function  A recursive function must have:      Base Case: A condition that stops the recursion.     Recursive Case: The part where the function calls itself with a modified argument.  2. Example: Factorial  The factorial of a number n is the product of all positive integers from 1 to n. Mathematically: n!=n×(n−1)×(n−2)…×1 n!=n×(n−1)×(n−2)…×1 Recursive Implementation:  def factorial(n):     # Base case: Stop recursion when n reaches 1     if n == 1:         return 1     # Recursive case: Call the function with n-1     else:         return n * factorial(n - 1)  # Test the function print(factorial(5))  # Output: 120  How it works:      factorial(5) calls factorial(4)     factorial(4) calls factorial(3) ...     Eventually, factorial(1) returns 1, stopping the recursion.  3. Example: Fibonacci Sequence  The Fibonacci sequence is: 0,1,1,2,3,5,8,… 0,1,1,2,3,5,8,…  Where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones. Recursive Implementation:  def fibonacci(n):     # Base cases     if n == 0:         return 0     elif n == 1:         return 1     # Recursive case     else:         return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)  # Test the function print(fibonacci(7))  # Output: 13  How it works:      fibonacci(7) calls fibonacci(6) and fibonacci(5), which then call smaller subproblems.  4. Key Points to Remember      Base Case is Critical: Without it, the function will run infinitely.     Performance: Recursive functions can be inefficient for large inputs because they might repeat calculations (like in Fibonacci). Solutions like memoization or iterative approaches can optimize this.     Depth Limit: Python has a recursion depth limit. You can check it using:      import sys     print(sys.getrecursionlimit())  5. Practice Problem: Sum of Digits  Write a recursive function to find the sum of the digits of a number.  def sum_of_digits(n):     # Base case     if n == 0:         return 0     # Recursive case     else:         return n % 10 + sum_of_digits(n // 10)  # Test the function print(sum_of_digits(123))  # Output: 6 (1 + 2 + 3)  Would you like more examples or practice problems? 😊

Mike sends an e-mail to Manager Ebony complaining that Marisol was a “flake" and has derailed the whole project. Marisol, meanwhile, meets with Ebony and complains that Mike was a jerk, is a "difficult person" and has put meeting the deadline in jeopardy. Manager Ebony is frustrated that this talented pair is having difficulty working together and  stressed about the other deadlines that her department is responsible for completing - yet seems to be destined to miss.  Ebony calls both Mike and Marisol into her office. She says, "I thought you two were the most talented marketing professionals on staff. I Statements help us to Assertively take responsibility for/and convey our wants/needs to the listener without blaming the listener.  I Statements Contain Four Steps (these can be in any order): A.  They state the facts of a situation (not perception of facts) B.  They convey interpretations of the observed situation C.  They convey at least one emotion D.  They specify the want/need and/or consequence SAMPLE I STATEMENT - MODEL YOURS TO INCLUDE ALL FOUR PARTS AS INDICATED BELOW: Factual Event:  You said last week you would cover my shift this Wednesday because I covered yours last Tuesday. (Emotion and Interpretation)  When we agreed to exchange shifts, I bought a plane ticket to attend my sister's wedding.  The ticket cannot be refunded and I need to be with my family at the wedding.  I would like us to sit down and talk through this in the next hour to figure out how we can get my shift covered, or I could lose my job.(want/ need and consequence are present) Notice how this statement states facts without blaming, owns the personal interpretation/emotions, avoids "you made me so frustrated" and states what is needed/wanted and why it's important. Gaie Delap, a retired teacher and Just Stop Oil protester, was sentenced to 20 months in prison for her participation in a climate protest on the M25 in 2022 and was released last November under the home detention curfew (HDC) scheme.    She was recalled to prison just before Christmas. Because of a history of deep-vein thrombosis, she could not have a tag attached to her ankle and no wrist tag that fitted her could be found.    People stand in front of Royal Courts of Justice  Keeping Gaie Delap in jail is a travesty of justice | Letters  Read more  On Friday she learned that the time she must spend in prison had been extended. Her supporters said she was shocked to receive a letter delivered to her cell saying that her time behind bars had been extended by 20 days as it corresponded to the period of time after she was notified of her recall to prison. During that time she had been at home with her suitcase packed, waiting to be arrested and reincarcerated.    Advertisement    Initially, Delap was informed she would be released on 17 March but on Friday she was told her release date had been delayed until 7 April.    The news emerged days after the Guardian revealed that the prisons minister, James Timpson, wants to reverse the rise in the number of women imprisoned, with more tagged and sent to rehabilitation centres.    Twenty-five legal, women’s and prison reform organisations and researchers have written to the justice secretary, Shabana Mahmood, calling on her to use her discretionary powers to revoke Delap’s recall, find a suitable tag for her to wear, and launch an inquiry into the systemic failures that led to this situation. Signatories to the letter include the Howard League for Penal Reform, the charity Women in Prison and the Good Law Project.    The letter questions the effectiveness of HDC, which is intended to reduce the prison population and allow individuals to reintegrate into society under supervised conditions.    “This is not a matter of public safety, as Ms Delap has demonstrated full compliance with her curfew terms. Her recall serves no purpose other than to exacerbate the punitive aspects of her sentence,” the letter states.    “In the interests of justice, humanity and effective public policy, we request you intervene immediately. Let this case serve as a catalyst for reforming the tagging system and ensuring that such situations do not recur.”    Advertisement    Delap’s brother, Mick Delap, said: “How come it has proved so impossible to fit this normal-sized woman, who desperately wants to have electronic monitoring, with any one of the many different forms of monitoring available to the authorities? What happened?    Gaie was sentenced to 20 months in prison for her participation in a climate protest in 2022.    She was released early under the Home Detention Curfew (HDC) scheme on 18th November 2024.    A warrant was put out for her on 5th December 2024 because Electronic Monitoring Services (EMS), operated by Serco, failed to fit her with an electronic tag.    Gaie could not be tagged on her ankle due to a history of deep vein thrombosis and the tag intended for her wrist was too large.    Despite fully complying with all curfew conditions and attempting to contact probation services, the prison, and the police to resolve the issue, Gaie was arrested on 21st December and recalled to prison.    As of 21st January, Gaie's sentence has now even been lengthened by another 20 days. The time that Gaie spent on bail waiting for the tag is being treated as time spent "unlawfully at large".    This shocking incarceration of Gaie does not just surface SERCO's inaptitude but also the sexism, ageism, and ableism inherent in a probation system that is not designed to serve women or older people with disabilities.          What are we asking from MPs?    We are calling for MPs to write to Justice Secretary Shabana Mahmood and request Gaie Delap's immediate release.    The tagging organisation EMS is employed by the state to do a job, and in Gaie’s case, it has failed.    It is the task of every MP to monitor the performance of executive organizations like EMS and to hold them to account. So it is appropriate for any MP to ask questions about EMS's service delivery, whether Gaie is their constituent or not.    We are NOT asking Shabana Mahmood or any MP to intervene in the sentencing process - there is an appeal on 29th/30th January which deals with that.    But as Lord Chancellor and Secretary of State for Justice, Shabana Mahmood, not a court, made the decision to recall Gaie. So she is the only person who can reverse this decision. llm_other: I never intentionally use chat bots, however every damned service in the world is trying to hop on the hyped-up and poorly designed bandwagon. When dealing with any form of customer service I have to navigate AROUND their damned useless chat bots to finally get to someone with a brain cell or two that can actually work around a real problem instead of just reciting the FAQ like a chat bot. I'm intelligent enough to not NEED help unless my particular circumstances place me into an edge case that an FAQ, a chat bot, or an automated process CAN'T FIX.  As for which of the danged useless garbage chat bots I've been forced to interact with, I couldn't tell you because I've never actually been informed what piece of garbage software I'm being handed off to.

comments: I understand that every business on the face of the Earth has to deal with hordes of brain-dead customers, daily, who can't be arsed to do the most basic research or even be trusted to find the company's website and click on the great big link in the middle of the page that will answer their question, and yes, I understand that handing these walking vegetables off to a chat bot to screen or herd is an efficient use of a business' resources, BUT FOR THE LOVE OF GOD stop assuming that a chat bot is capable of doing much beyond reciting a FAQ or doing basic call screening for your actual customer service representatives. Large language models do not, and will not for the foreseeable future, have the ability to replace line-level customer service employees or perform even the most basic customer-faced interactions without royally fucking up even MORE than a drugged-up high-school dropout call-center hire.

comments: I don't know where to start here. AI is still in its early stages and people are both optimistic and fearful about its potential. People are both frustrated with AI's inaccuracies and the fact that it doesn't seem to know everything from the onset of its existence. While also being fearful of its all-knowing, all-seeing Skynet people replacing, famine causing future. It all really doesn't make a whole lot of sense to me because those fears are often overblown. Especially when those in the media, that have no background in anything technological start fearmongering. It harkens back to when the Today show hosts were musing to each other "have you heard of this internet?" Ai is a tool, currently it is very helpful to me and will become more helpful in the future. It makes learning easier and more streamlined. It gives me information and places to look further to understanding the topics that I am interested in. I understand Ai's potential and have to parse the bullshit coming from people that are all shouting into the void about its negative consequences. I have to figure out which of those voices aren't just imbeciles barking nonsense and which of those are genuine inevitabilities. Nonetheless, AI is here to stay, and I will be utilizing it to the best I can. You either have to adapt to and understand the technology that controls our lives otherwise you are at a disadvantage.
